question.text: A conducting circular loop is placed in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>Y</mi></math> plane in presence of magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover accent="true"><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced></math> in SI unit. If the radius of the loop is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, the induced emf in the loop, at time, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mi>π</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
By the faraday's law in electromagnetic induction

εind=-dϕdt=-dB→·A→dt

Magnetic flux is ϕ=B→·A→=3t3j^+3t2k^·π12k^

So, ϕ=3t2π

Now, induced emf is εind=dϕdt=6tπ

At t=2, εind=62π=12π V.

Thus, the value of n=12.
